evals.prompt: In an ESIMD kernel for Intel Xe2, how do I split a work-group barrier into a separate signal and wait, so that independent work can run between them? Show the calls.
evals.expected_output: Named barriers in sycl::ext::intel::esimd: named_barrier_init<N>() at kernel start declares N barriers; every thread calls named_barrier_signal(id, 0, num_threads, num_threads) after its SLM writes, does independent work (global loads, prefetches, register-only math) that touches no shared SLM, then calls named_barrier_wait(id) before reading other threads' SLM data. There is no nbarrier class in the ESIMD headers.

evals.prompt: An existing ESIMD kernel calls __esimd_nbarrier_init(1), __esimd_nbarrier_arrive(0, 0, 32, 32) and __esimd_nbarrier(0, 0, 32). What are the equivalent public ESIMD functions, and what do the arguments mean?
evals.expected_output: __esimd_nbarrier_init(1) is named_barrier_init<1>() (one named barrier). __esimd_nbarrier_arrive(0, 0, 32, 32) is named_barrier_signal(0, 0, 32, 32): barrier id 0, mode 0, 32 producers, 32 consumers; the public function also issues a fence first. __esimd_nbarrier(0, 0, 32) is named_barrier_wait(0): the first argument 0 selects wait, the second is the barrier id.
